description:
CI RED on Linux; passes on macOS.

    matrix::extern_float_lanes::interp  dlsym: symbol `sqrt` not found
    matrix::extern_float_lanes::run     FAILED
    matrix::extern_float_lanes::build   /usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `pow\'
                                        /usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `jn\'

On macOS the math functions live inside libSystem, which is already loaded and
already linked, so declaring `extern "C" fn sqrt` just works. On Linux they
live in libm: dlsym over the default namespace does not find them for the interp
and JIT doors, and the AOT link line has no -lm for the build door.

TWO THINGS, and they should be separated:

  * sqrt/pow are C99 and portable. The fixture is legitimate; what is missing is
    that fz has no way to say which library an extern comes from, and no -lm on
    the AOT link line.

  * `jn` (Bessel of order n) is an XSI/BSD extension. It was chosen to exercise
    a three-argument float shape (fz-5xp.37) and is not worth a portability
    dependency; pick a C99 function of the same shape (fma) instead.

This is the same class as the sibling ticket about the JIT symbol table: a
symbol resolving by accident on the development platform.
title: extern_float_lanes depends on libm symbols that only resolve on macOS
